title: How policymakers’ speeches and interviews move markets
gist: New ECB research using a database of ~5,000 inter-meeting speeches and interviews (1999-2024) finds that policymakers' informal communication between Governing Council meetings moves euro area markets nearly as much in cumulative terms as formal policy announcements, especially at longer maturities, and produces sharper, more statistically significant estimates of monetary policy's effect on unemployment and inflation than formal announcements alone.

themes.theme: A new database of ECB communication

insights.claim: Researchers built the Euro Area Communication Event Study Database (EA-CED), covering 304 formal Governing Council policy announcements and around 5,000 inter-meeting speeches and interviews from January 1999 to early 2024, including communication from ECB Presidents, Executive Board members, and the central bank governors of Germany, France, Spain, and Italy.
insights.speaker: Klodiana Istrefi, Florens Odendahl, and Giulia Sestieri
insights.so_what: A ~5,000-event database spanning 25 years gives market analysts and macro researchers a far larger, systematized dataset than formal-announcement-only studies for building trading or forecasting models around ECB communication.
insights.quote: It includes 304 formal policy announcements following Governing Council monetary policy meetings and around 5,000 public communication events that took place between Governing Council meetings from January 1999 to early 2024.
insights.locator: A new database of communication between

insights.claim: Market reactions were measured as the difference between the median asset price quote in the 15 minutes after a communication event and the 15 minutes before it, compared against typical background market volatility to isolate genuine 'surprise' reactions.
insights.speaker: Klodiana Istrefi, Florens Odendahl, and Giulia Sestieri
insights.so_what: This narrow-window, volatility-adjusted event-study method is a replicable methodology traders or researchers could apply to other central banks' inter-meeting communications to build similar surprise-reaction datasets.
insights.quote: we take the difference between the median quote of each financial variable in the 15 minutes after the event... and the 15 minutes before the event

themes.theme: Inter-meeting communication moves markets almost as much as formal decisions

insights.claim: Around 45% of formal ECB policy announcements produced a significant market reaction, versus a smaller share of individual inter-meeting communication events, but because there are far more speeches and interviews than formal announcements, their cumulative market impact is comparable.
insights.speaker: Klodiana Istrefi, Florens Odendahl, and Giulia Sestieri
insights.so_what: Traders and macro analysts focused only on scheduled Governing Council decisions are missing roughly half the market-moving informal-communication events, an information-coverage gap that a systematic monitoring approach could close.
insights.quote: around 45% of formal policy announcements produced a significant market reaction. By contrast, the results from inter-meeting communication events were more diverse and a smaller share of them generated a significant market reaction.

insights.claim: More than 300 inter-meeting communication events generated a significant Euro Stoxx 50 reaction versus 117 formal policy announcements, and cumulatively these events moved the index by 273 percentage points versus 98 percentage points for formal announcements.
insights.speaker: Klodiana Istrefi, Florens Odendahl, and Giulia Sestieri
insights.so_what: Inter-meeting speeches moving the Euro Stoxx 50 nearly 3x more in cumulative terms than scheduled decisions is a concrete, tradable signal that equity strategists should weight unscheduled ECB speeches as seriously as the policy calendar itself.
insights.quote: more than 300 inter-meeting communication events generated a significant reaction in the Euro Stoxx 50 index, compared with 117 formal policy announcements. Taken together, these events moved the index by 273 percentage points in cumulative terms.

insights.claim: For the two-year OIS rate, cumulative effects of formal announcements (718 basis points) and inter-meeting communication (681 basis points) were similar over 1999-2024, and at longer maturities inter-meeting communication events become more influential, with cumulative effects up to twice as large as formal announcements.
insights.speaker: Klodiana Istrefi, Florens Odendahl, and Giulia Sestieri
insights.so_what: The finding that speeches dominate at longer maturities means fixed-income desks pricing longer-dated euro rates should treat ECB speech calendars as a primary input, not a secondary one, for long-end rate expectations.
insights.quote: At longer maturities, inter-meeting communication events become more influential, with cumulative effects up to twice as large as those of formal policy announcements.
insights.locator: Overall, in terms of cumulative effects

themes.theme: Case studies of individual speeches moving markets

insights.claim: Jean-Claude Trichet's November 2005 Frankfurt speech, in which he said the ECB 'will remove some of the accommodation' in policy, sharply moved the one-year OIS rate and signaled the ECB's first rate hike in five years, delivered the following month.
insights.speaker: Klodiana Istrefi, Florens Odendahl, and Giulia Sestieri
insights.so_what: This is a concrete historical case of a single unscheduled speech correctly pre-signaling a rate hike a month before the formal decision, validating that ECB speech language is a leading indicator worth trading on.
insights.quote: We will remove some of the accommodation which is in the present monetary policy stance

insights.claim: Mario Draghi's June 2019 Sintra speech, warning that 'additional stimulus will be required' absent an inflation improvement, sharply lowered the one-year OIS rate and preceded a September 2019 deposit rate cut to -0.50% and the restart of net asset purchases.
insights.speaker: Klodiana Istrefi, Florens Odendahl, and Giulia Sestieri
insights.so_what: A second concrete case shows the same speech-to-policy-action pattern for an easing cycle, reinforcing the leading-indicator value of ECB Forum speeches specifically as a venue to watch for policy pivots.
insights.quote: In the absence of improvement, such that the sustained return of inflation to our aim is threatened, additional stimulus will be required

insights.claim: Christine Lagarde's November 2021 Frankfurt speech, stating conditions for a rate hike were 'very unlikely' to be met in 2022 and warning against premature tightening, lowered the one-year OIS rate and the euro.
insights.speaker: Klodiana Istrefi, Florens Odendahl, and Giulia Sestieri
insights.so_what: A third case extends the pattern to FX markets, showing speech-driven repricing isn't limited to rates but also moves the euro directly, relevant to FX desks tracking ECB rhetoric alongside rates traders.
insights.quote: the conditions to raise rates are very unlikely to be satisfied next year

themes.theme: Speeches pre-signal the direction of the next decision, asymmetrically

insights.claim: In the weeks before a Governing Council meeting, speeches shift OIS rates in the same direction as the eventual decision: before rate hikes, speeches push rates up; before rate cuts, they push rates down, but less strongly.
insights.speaker: Klodiana Istrefi, Florens Odendahl, and Giulia Sestieri
insights.so_what: This gives traders a directional pre-meeting signal to watch for, and the built-in asymmetry (stronger signaling before hikes) means a lack of vocal pre-signaling ahead of a meeting is itself weak evidence against an imminent hike.
insights.quote: Before rate hikes, speeches and interviews push rates upwards. Before rate cuts, they push rates downwards, albeit more modestly.
insights.locator: In fact, in the weeks before

insights.claim: The asymmetry between stronger pre-hike and weaker pre-cut signaling suggests Governing Council members increase the strength of their communication more ahead of monetary tightening (signaling inflation vigilance) than ahead of easing.
insights.speaker: Klodiana Istrefi, Florens Odendahl, and Giulia Sestieri
insights.so_what: This implies ECB communication strategy itself is asymmetric by design (louder on hawkishness than dovishness), a behavioral pattern that should be priced into how much weight markets give to ambiguous or muted pre-meeting rhetoric.
insights.quote: This asymmetry suggests that Governing Council members increase the strength of their communication more ahead of monetary policy tightening—signalling vigilance on inflation—than ahead of monetary policy easing.

themes.theme: Which speakers move markets the most

insights.claim: The average impact on the two-year OIS rate from 1999-2024 was 5.13 basis points for formal policy announcements, versus 2.56 bps for ECB President speeches, 2.14 bps for Executive Board member speeches, 2.42 bps for the four largest national central bank governors, and 2.62 bps for interviews across these policymakers — making the ECB President the most impactful inter-meeting speaker, closely followed by the national central bank governors.
insights.speaker: Klodiana Istrefi, Florens Odendahl, and Giulia Sestieri
insights.so_what: That national central bank governors (Bundesbank, Banque de France, Banco de España, Banca d'Italia) rank nearly as impactful as the ECB President is a specific, actionable finding for market-communication monitoring teams who might otherwise track only the ECB President and Executive Board.
insights.quote: the ECB President has the largest impact on average, followed closely by the President and Governors of the four NCBs and then the ECB Executive Board members

themes.theme: Better estimates of monetary policy's real-economy effects

insights.claim: Using a Bayesian vector autoregression model, estimates of monetary policy's effect on unemployment and inflation based on inter-meeting communication surprises were more statistically precise (tighter confidence bands) than estimates based on formal policy announcements alone, where the unemployment response was statistically insignificant.
insights.speaker: Klodiana Istrefi, Florens Odendahl, and Giulia Sestieri
insights.so_what: This means economists estimating the real-economy impact of ECB policy using only scheduled-announcement data are working with weaker, statistically insignificant unemployment estimates, and should incorporate inter-meeting communication surprises to get reliable results.
insights.quote: the unemployment response is statistically insignificant... the effects are clearer and more significant when using information from inter-meeting communication events
insights.locator: When we base the information in the model
